<!-- pr-reviewer: 1299e7123cfd030e28782d208cc4c0e49208260b -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (focused review of the #379 change only, not the full suite).

**What looks good**
- The reasoning holds: the OS API is process-global, `ensure_initialized` writes after releasing its mutex, so finishing it once under `std::sync::Once` before the first `World::new` closes the window. Every other thread blocks in `call_once` until it is done.
- Every world-creation path goes through it. A grep of `crates/` (app, ui, tests, helpers) finds `World::new` only inside `new_world()` (`crates/app/src/world.rs`).
- No `unsafe` added. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the library code; the `expect`s are in the test only. No Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock change. Provenance line and decision file are present.
- The new test re-runs its own binary as child processes. Each child releases 32 threads at a barrier to build their first worlds, with CPU spinners adding load. That is the right shape, because the race only exists on a process's first worlds. It is bounded (no hang) and fails with the children's output.

**Local results (merged with current origin/main, clean merge)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test world_init_race`: 5 of 5 runs passed (about 16-17 s each in debug)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test scripting`: 17 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib world`: no tests match the filter (0 run)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The test is a stress test, so a pass is evidence, not proof. The PR says so itself.
- At about 16 s in debug it is above the usual quick-tier feel. It is one test, so the cost is bounded, but the maintainer may want it in a slower lane later.
- `cargo test --lib world` finds no tests, so the Once itself is covered only by the integration test.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
